answer.held_back_by: Honestly I don't think anything did. I ended as PM with integrity 100, so the game mostly rewarded being decent. The only thing holding me back was the party's estimate of Minister, which I didn't know about until the end.
answer.ending_fair_why: Yes, it made sense. Listening to the nominated officer was the big choice and it paid off. But I only found out afterwards that this was the turning point, so it felt a bit hidden.
answer.chase_next: The one where I take the conglomerate board seat. I turned it down and want to see if I get rich and what the game says about it, probably a worse ending but more fun to see.
answer.play_again_why: It was good but a long run, and the years in the middle blurred together. I'd come back another day for the board seat path.

tone_breaks.line: Director winked when I stayed silent
tone_breaks.note: Funny, but it felt a little like the game nudging me, not an actual workplace moment.
The tone shifts to a bit smug in the ending card. The reveal that the party's estimate was Minister was neat but the wording is cheeky.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is about whether your work and character hold up, not the pay. The salary is only a line on the card each year, so Confirmed & Substantive fits better, even if I only half understand the term.

finalScreen:
DARREN LIM · THE FINAL POSITION
Prime Minister

You made it. The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary, and the formula was published, so nobody can say they were not told.

RETIRED AS Prime Minister
AT AGE 59
LIFETIME EARNINGS $38.32M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.
THE PARTY'S ESTIMATE: When you won your seat, the party made its own: Minister. Nobody told you that either.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 38, in The Officer You Nominated, you chose "Let her decide without hearing from you." It raised your ceiling to Prime Minister.
EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
